L1.text: Every Sunday, Little Red Riding Hood brought her grandma a cake. And every Sunday, the big bad wolf got a little bit fatter.

L2.text: At first, nobody noticed. I mean, wolves eat a lot, right?

L3.text: But after a month, the wolf couldn't fit through the door of his own cave.

L4.text: Red got suspicious. Grandma said she loved the cakes. But grandma never got any bigger.

L5.text: So Red asks the hunter for help.

L6.text: The hunter looks at the wolf. Then at Red. And goes: so your problem is a fat wolf?

L7.text: He laughs all the way back into the forest.

L8.text: So one night, Red hides in grandma's closet. And waits.

L9.text: Three a.m. The front door creaks open.

L10.text: The wolf squeezes inside. And grandma is already waiting for him. With a fork.

L11.text: But she doesn't take a single bite. She feeds him. Every crumb. Every single cake.

L12.text: Because grandma knew exactly how dangerous that wolf was.

L13.text: And a wolf this fat can't chase anyone.

L14.text: For five years, grandma hasn't eaten a single piece of cake.

L15.text: And Red Riding Hood? Has never been safer.
